inputs.original_text: The promises of Rs 2,000 a month for women, Rs 8,000 in household coupons, and free motor pumpsets for farmers may offer immediate help, with more support for fishermen and jobs also on the table. But relief should strengthen families and productive livelihoods—not become a substitute for them. The real test is whether people can build secure lives through work, farming, and local enterprise, rather than being kept dependent on political promises. FDI and AI aren’t inherently the enemy; they should serve the country and its people, not be pursued at the expense of them.
inputs.modified_text: Rs 2,000 a month for women, Rs 8,000 in household coupons and free motor pumpsets for farmers may ease pressure now, with more support for fishermen and jobs also on the table. But handouts are no substitute for families, steady work and livelihoods people can sustain with dignity. A government should help citizens stand on their own feet, not make them dependent on political promises. FDI and AI should strengthen the country and its people—not be treated as ends in themselves or allowed to displace the interests of ordinary families and local enterprise.
